cards.tip: Press your lips together, then open with a tiny voiced puff. Keep it short; avoid adding “uh”.
Press your lips together, then release a small puff of air. Voice stays off.
Close your lips and hum. Feel the buzz with your fingers on your throat.
Tap your tongue just behind your top teeth, then release. Keep it short.
Tap your tongue just behind your top teeth. Turn your voice on.
Put your tongue behind your top teeth and hum through your nose.
Lift the back of your tongue, then release a little puff. Voice stays off.
Lift the back of your tongue, then release. Turn your voice on.
Rest your top teeth gently on your bottom lip. Blow softly.
Rest your top teeth on your bottom lip and blow with your voice on.
Keep your teeth close and send air out in a smooth hiss.
Make a smooth buzzing sound with teeth close and voice on.
Open your mouth and gently breathe out.
Round your lips, turn your voice on, then open your lips.
Lift the middle of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth, then glide away.
Lift and pull your tongue back without touching the roof. Keep your voice on.
Touch your tongue just behind your top teeth and use your voice.
Round your lips a little and blow a quiet “shhh”.
Start with your tongue up, then release a quick puff with rounded lips.
Make the quick mouth motion for ch, but add your voice.
Put the tip of your tongue gently between your teeth and blow. No voice.
Put the tip of your tongue gently between your teeth. Blow with your voice on.
Lift the back of your tongue and hum through your nose. No extra g sound.
Make the mouth shape for sh and add a gentle buzz with your voice.
Open your mouth wide, with your tongue low toward the front.
Open your mouth a little with your tongue relaxed toward the front.
Keep your mouth relaxed and slightly open. Keep the vowel short.
Open your mouth with your jaw down and your tongue low. Accent may change this vowel.
Relax your lips and open your mouth a little. Make a short central vowel.
Start with your mouth partly open, then glide toward a smile.
Smile gently and lift your tongue toward the front of your mouth.
Open your mouth, then glide toward a smile.
Start with your mouth open, then round your lips as you glide.
Start with a y glide, then round your lips for oo. Often taught as long u; it combines sounds.
Round your lips and lift the back of your tongue. Hold a smooth vowel.
Round your lips loosely. Keep the vowel short and relaxed.
Open your mouth, then glide into rounded lips.
Begin with rounded lips, then glide toward a smile.
Open your mouth, then pull your tongue back for r.
Round your lips, then move into the r sound.
Lift and pull your tongue back. Your lips may round a little.
Begin with an open front vowel and glide into r.
Start with an ee-like vowel and glide into r.
Open your mouth and relax your jaw. Keep the sound smooth.
Blend k straight into w. Two sounds, smoothly together.
Blend k straight into s. Two sounds, smoothly together.
